subject: URGENT: Halcyon - elevated 504s & throughput drop (us-west2) / request for cross-region diversion
messages:
From: James Hunter <james.hunter@halcyonretail.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Karina Perez <kperez@halcyonretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: Halcyon - increased 504s and token latency in us-west2

Aditya —

We started seeing a large spike in 504s and per-token latency on our checkout endpoints at ~08:50 PDT this morning. Our engineering team has measured:
- 504 rate jumped from ~0.05% to ~4.2% between 08:50–09:05
- p95 token latency increased from ~120ms to ~420ms for requests pinned to us-west2
- Throughput dropped roughly 35% for heavy payloads (>=2k tokens)

This is directly affecting our checkout funnel (cart conversions down ~9% over the past 20 minutes). We have partial traffic failover in our app but users still hit the Redwood API and see errors. We need an immediate plan: can you confirm whether this is a regional issue and whether you can divert traffic to another region (us-west1 / us-east1)?

Attached: small sample of the 504 responses and timing traces.

—James
James Hunter
VP Engineering, Halcyon Retail
Attachment: halcyon-error-sample.log (text/plain, 48KB)

Attachments: halcyon-error-sample.log (from customer).

—Aditya

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: URGENT: Halcyon - increased 504s and token latency in us-west2

Digging in — preliminary triage below.

What we see:
- Metrics show a fabric flap in us-west2-a starting ~08:48 PDT; packet loss/latency on ~38% of serving nodes causing elevated 5xxs and token-level slowdowns.
- Workload mix: Halcyon uses a lot of long-sequence generation; those requests are most sensitive to KV cache misses.

Immediate mitigation recommendation (emergency playbook):
1) Apply traffic steering: shift 65% of Halcyon's traffic away from us-west2 to a mix of us-west1 (45%) and us-east1 (20%) using emergency routing weights. Command (operator): redwood route set --account=HAL-2025-042 --region us-west1 --weight 0.45 --policy emergency; and repeat for us-east1.
2) Keep 35% pinned to us-west2 for cache-warmth and to reduce cold-start amplification.
3) Monitor token latencies and 5xxs for 5 minutes; if error rate <=0.5% and p95 latency stabilizes, gradually move to normal failover policy.
4) If errors persist, escalate to full evacuate and redistribute KV caches (this is heavier and will take ~20–30m).

Estimated impact: expected p95 increase of ~30–50ms for diverted requests; throughput should recover to ~90% of baseline within 6–10 minutes after weights change.

Attachments: us-west2-routing-plan.pdf (detailed step sequence, rollback commands). Runbook: https://redwood-internal.prod/runbooks/us-west2-failover

Risk notes:
- Some EU customers may see marginally worse latency if routed to us-east1.
- If we divert too aggressively we increase cache misses and token cost for Halcyon; Rishi can advise on model-level mitigations.

If we need to do the steer now, I recommend getting exec consent for the temporary cross-region traffic shift and the customer-facing credit.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE Lead, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: URGENT: Halcyon - increased 504s and token latency in us-west2

James —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for sending the log sample. We’re treating this as a P1. Our SREs recommend an emergency diversion off us-west2 to us-west1/us-east1 to restore throughput and reduce 5xxs. Hannah included the exact plan and rollback steps.

Customer-facing plan:
- We will request a 20-minute exec sync on this thread for immediate approval to steer traffic. Can you join a quick call at 9:40 PDT?
- Proposed mitigation: implement partial diversion (65% away from us-west2) immediately; monitor for stabilization.
- To make Halcyon whole for the customer impact window we are prepared to offer a one-time credit — proposed 10% of this month’s invoice for the impacted window; we can adjust based on final scope.

Can you confirm you’re comfortable with the diversion and the proposed credit? If yes, we’ll proceed after internal exec sign-off.

—Marissa
